title: Three Fridays and One Short Card
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：joke　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 joke 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1985 the friend ① told the joke that no stranger in the canteen would have recorded, and he said the telling was the whole of the Friday. The ② joke, meaning the laugh itself and not the card, ran three Fridays and stayed unrecorded in the book; a joke, he said, is the only thing in a canteen that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ joke in that canteen had the same short card beside it, and the ④ joke at the far table, meaning the story they kept for the children to tell and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A joke, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the friend said the recording is the part that fills three Fridays.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the joke was the whole of the matter, meaning the mood and not the laugh. The ⑥ joke, meaning the mood and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; joke, he said, is either something you tell or the only word that means both a laugh and a mood. He said the mood is the part they remember.

By 1990 the ⑦ joke had become a line in a note, and the note had become an argument about the short card. The ⑧ joke of the whole thing, the friend wrote in June, was one canteen and three Fridays of recording; joke, he said, is either the story at the far table or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ joke I remember is the laugh recorded in the note, which closed in 1992 and is still recorded as the quietest in the canteen. A ⑩ joke, my mother said in 1994, is the only laugh that improves by being recorded; every joke, she said, is a mood that has agreed to look like a laugh. She said the mood was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 笑话；玩笑（指食堂里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 笑话；玩笑（指那个笑料本身，与卡片相对）
C. 固定搭配：tell the joke 讲这个笑话
D. n. 笑话；玩笑（指留给孩子们讲的那一个那一个）
E. n. 谐趣之事（抽象总称，指一处食堂的笑话之事）
F. n. 笑话；玩笑（指便条里写到、被记下的的那一个）
G. n. 心情、调剂（指一件事里人人都笑却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 调剂（抽象总称，指人人都笑却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: told the joke that no stranger in the canteen would have recorded
The joke, meaning the laugh itself and not the card
the joke at the far table
the joke was the whole of the matter
the joke had become a line in a note
The joke of the whole thing
A joke, my mother said in 1994

answers.why: tell the joke 意为“讲这个笑话”，1985 年那位朋友把食堂里没有一位陌生人肯记录的一个笑话做了一遍。
joke 意为“笑话；玩笑”，指那个笑料本身而不是卡片，它经过了三个星期五而在簿子上没有被记录。
joke 意为“笑话；玩笑”，指食堂里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一张薄薄的卡片。
joke 意为“笑话；玩笑”，指最远那张桌边留给孩子们讲的那一个那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
joke 意为“心情、调剂”，指一件事里人人都笑却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份心情就是那件事的全部。
joke 意为“调剂”，指人人都笑却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个笑料，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
joke 意为“笑话；玩笑”，指便条里写到、被记下的的那一个，到 1990 年这一个成了便条里的一行。
joke 意为“谐趣之事”，朋友六月写道，整件事的笑话之事是一处食堂和三个星期五的记录。
joke 意为“笑话；玩笑”，我记得的是便条里记录过的那一个，1992 年讲完了，至今仍被说成食堂里最安静的一个。
joke 为抽象总称，母亲 1994 年说，笑话是唯一会因为被好好记录而变得更好的笑料。
